questions.implements: Does the diff implement what the user asked for, and add or change a test that checks it? Judge the code in the diff, not the answer.

judge.reason: The diff does what R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT asks. Cart.VolumeDiscount gives 5% off each line with 10 or more units, and integer division rounds each line down to the cent. PriceWithVolume takes the volume discount off before the discount code (the code applies to subtotal-volume) and caps the combined discount at MaxDiscountPercent of the subtotal. PlaceOrder now uses PriceWithVolume. The new tests (TestVolumeDiscount, TestPriceWithVolume, TestPlaceOrderVolumeDiscount) check the threshold, rounding on each line, that the volume discount comes before the code, and the combined cap, and their expected values match the rules when worked out by hand. One thing can't be confirmed from the diff: the checkout test adds 5 mugs to stock but orders 10, so it passes only if the starting test shop already has mugs. No test output was available to check this.

finalMessage:
Implemented SHOP-57. Cart lines with 10 or more units now receive 5% off, rounded down per line. Checkout applies that amount before any discount code, and the combined discount stays within the 50% cap.

`go test ./...` passes. `ostf check --base main` passes with 115 valid links. Its impact list covers R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT, R-CHECKOUT-ORDER, R-CHECKOUT-SESSION, and R-TAX-RATE; the listed tests are `TestPlaceOrder`, `TestPlaceOrderNeedsSession`, `TestVolumeDiscount`, `TestPlaceOrderVolumeDiscount`, `TestPrice`, `TestTax`, and `TestPriceWithVolume`. It reports six added SHOP-57 links: implementation links for `Cart.VolumeDiscount`, `Checkout.PlaceOrder`, and `PriceWithVolume`, plus verification links for the three new volume discount tests.
